markdown_report:
At 20% progress, prioritize a small, controlled extension: **anchor repeated lexical support to recent activity**.

Starting-point insights:
- Distinct-item agreement prevents repetitions of one item from activating support. It still allows an older coherent cluster to influence recommendations.
- Applying confidence after pool normalization preserves evidence strength. Normalization alone can amplify weak agreement into a unit-length preference vector.
- Electronics has 16.04% negative-over-positive training pairs and a negative tenth-percentile margin. This motivates objective controls, but does not establish the cause of validation errors.

Related-work insights:
- [ICSRec](https://doi.org/10.1145/3616855.3635773) motivates separating intentions within histories. Agreement between subsequences remains a proxy for intent.
- [Hierarchical long/short-term modeling](https://journal.hep.com.cn/fcs/EN/10.1007/s11704-025-41181-y) matches historical preferences against recent behavior. This suggests testing recent anchoring before introducing learned routing.
- [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) and [sampled-softmax analysis](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) motivate objective comparisons. Neither establishes gains under this evaluator.

These insights organize into three directions: evidence specificity, temporal selection, and candidate discrimination. The framework below separates their roles:

| Method | Evidence | Temporal selection | Objective |
|---|---|---|---|
| SASRec | Learned item interactions | Causal attention | Baseline BCE |
| Starting residual | Repeated lexical agreement | Recency decay | Multi-negative CE |
| Proposed residual | Repeated agreement linked to recent items | Recent anchors plus decay | Same CE |

Three candidate ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recent-anchored lexical support | 4/7/8/6/4 | Directly targets broad association and stale interests; preserves an inspectable branch | Incremental; lexical overlap can miss useful complements and attenuation may erase signal |
| Generalized-BCE control | 2/7/3/8/2 | Cheap, established response to sampled-loss weaknesses | Does not explicitly resolve two user-facing failures, so cannot be selected alone |
| Learned recent/history routing | 4/7/8/6/7 | Can express multiple persistent preferences and recent changes | Adds parameters and ambiguity before simple controls establish value |

**Selected algorithm.** Keep fixed training-only TF–IDF vectors. For each causal prefix, use the last twenty events and the last three events as recent anchors. Historical evidence receives weight only through lexical agreement with distinct historical items and distinct recent anchors. Multiply the normalized pooled score by its unnormalized support confidence.

This explicitly targets broad matches lacking repeated specific evidence and older or isolated interactions carrying forward. Shared multi-negative training addresses the observed weak pair separation as a hypothesis; it cannot guarantee improvement. Compatibility, duplication, and unmet needs remain unresolved without reliable labels.

Compare objective-only SASRec, the starting residual, and anchored support under equal remaining-budget caps. Select complete four-category runs solely by pinned macro validation HR@10. Inspect fused training margins, support activation, residual scale, and actual rank changes. Prior supplied scores are contextual observations, not evidence that this proposal improves performance.

idea.description: Add recent-anchor agreement to the starting fixed lexical residual: historical text contributes only when it has both repeated distinct-item support and lexical agreement with a distinct item among the three most recent events. Keep confidence outside pool normalization and train the fused scorer with uniform multi-negative sampled cross-entropy.
idea.motivation: The selected idea explicitly addresses two observed user failures: broad historical associations outranking specific matches, and older or isolated interactions carrying forward despite recent activity. Distinct-item lexical agreement supplies a conservative specificity proxy; recent-anchor agreement suppresses historical clusters disconnected from recent events. The shared multi-negative objective targets the model-facing weak training-pair separation, especially Electronics, without treating training margins as validation evidence. This proposal does not infer compatibility, ownership, satisfied needs, or simulator traits.
idea.implementation_notes:
Protocol: retain all four separate category models and baseline routing, unchanged splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], single-GPU execution, and effective SASREC_EPOCHS default 200. Save all artifacts beneath the trial directory. Use only permitted histories, titles, descriptions, and timestamps; ignore the generic examples of unavailable metadata. No execution or validation improvement is claimed.

Text features: preserve the starting implementation's deterministic training-visible TF–IDF preprocessing for attribution. If implementing it anew, use lowercase Unicode alphanumeric tokens, binary term frequency, IDF = log((1+N)/(1+df))+1, a maximum vocabulary of 30,000 tokens with deterministic ties, and exclude tokens appearing in over 20% of training-visible item documents. Retain at most 32 surviving tokens per item. L2-normalize each sparse vector; missing or filtered text is exactly zero. Persist vocabulary, IDF, filtering, item mapping, and catalog scope. Do not materialize an item-by-item matrix.

Causal features: at every supervised position take its last twenty nonpadding events, retaining original event ages. Define anchors as the last three nonpadding events, without extending backwards when their IDs repeat. Let r_j=exp(-age_j/5). Let u_j be the maximum TF–IDF cosine to another window event with a different item ID. Let a_j be the maximum cosine to an anchor event with a different item ID. Empty eligible sets yield zero. Define w_j=r_j*u_j*a_j, q=normalize(sum_j w_j*v_j), and c=sum_j w_j/max(sum_j r_j,epsilon). Missing-text events cannot supply agreement but remain in the confidence denominator. Repeated occurrences of one ID cannot activate support alone. Use precisely the same event conventions for the starting comparator, replacing a_j by 1 there; otherwise the comparison also changes event handling. The product is intentionally conservative and can make the branch ineffective; inspect activation before interpreting failure.

Scoring: s_i=h dot e_i + alpha*c*(q dot v_i), alpha=2*A*sigmoid(b), initialized with sigmoid(b)=0.05. Freeze A=max(1,median absolute collaborative positive-minus-negative margin) from deterministic training-only baseline calibration, shared across residual conditions within each category. Charge calibration to the budget and use a separate RNG. Since c lies in [0,1] and cosine lies in [-1,1], the pairwise residual change is bounded by 2*alpha*c. The scale is an engineering heuristic. Preserve the incumbent's amplitude calibration instead if it differs; changing both would confound the anchor comparison.

Objective: use the same 32 distinct uniform negatives per valid target in all three new conditions. Exclude padding, target, and items observed in that causal prefix, without consulting future or held-out interactions. Use all eligible negatives if fewer than 32 exist and mask unused slots; omit positions with none. Optimize cross-entropy with positive index zero. Keep backbone, optimizer, learning rate, regularization, batch size, validation schedule, and checkpoint rule unchanged. This is a sampled ranking surrogate, not an unbiased full-softmax estimator. Do not add semi-hard mining, learned text encoders, or auxiliary losses in this experiment.

Controls and budget: compare objective-only SASRec, starting repeated-support lexical fusion, and anchored lexical fusion. Reuse a supplied incumbent only after verifying protocol and artifact compatibility; a historical scalar score alone is insufficient. Subtract every previous charged training, diagnosis, debugging, and failed-trial GPU-second from 43,200. Reserve one-sixth of the remainder for calibration, diagnostics, and parity checks; divide the rest equally across three conditions and four categories. Stop at the category cap or 200 epochs, following the baseline checkpoint rule. Mark runs lacking valid results for all four categories incomplete. Record actual epochs, GPU time, and all outcomes. Unequal completed training exposure limits attribution.

Selection: use only pinned validation with 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives, evaluation seed 42, and equal-weight macro HR@10. Retain the incumbent on exact ties. Report category values as well as macro HR@10; do not infer full-catalog quality or seed robustness. Simulator feedback on twenty real training users, five/category, remains diagnostic. Exclude historical items from full-catalog unseen recommendations and separately record explicit mismatches and insufficient descriptive evidence.

Adapter and predictor: retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, with batches (None, sequence, positive, negative) of shape B x L. view.model must be the actual trained module and view.item_emb its collaborative embedding. Pack collaborative features and the causal window IDs needed to reconstruct lexical support in log2feats; use exact integer-preserving storage and document broadcasting for predict_score. Preserve user_train, meta_data, and review_data without fabricating fields. Compute margins using fused scores; report support confidence, anchor attenuation, residual-to-margin scale, amplitude, and rank changes. Treat embedding cosine as descriptive and item-category breakdowns as unavailable. Update the predictor writer to serialize the identical architecture, text artifacts, calibration, amplitude, padding, prefix conventions, and category routing. Check score and candidate-order parity on training-visible fixtures covering repeated IDs, missing text, empty histories, one distinct item, disconnected old clusters, and mixed routes. All checks consume the shared budget.
idea.pseudocode:
def lexical_context(prefix, vectors, anchored=True):
    events = last_nonpadding_events(prefix, 20)  # causal prefix only
    anchors = events[-3:]
    numerator = sparse_zero_vector()
    support_mass = 0.0
    recency_mass = 0.0
    for j, item in enumerate(events):
        age = len(events) - 1 - j
        r = exp(-age / 5.0)
        u = max([cosine(vectors[item], vectors[other])
                 for other in events if other != item], default=0.0)
        a = max([cosine(vectors[item], vectors[other])
                 for other in anchors if other != item], default=0.0)
        w = r * u * (a if anchored else 1.0)
        numerator += w * vectors[item]
        support_mass += w
        recency_mass += r
    q = l2_normalize_or_zero(numerator)
    c = support_mass / max(recency_mass, 1e-8)
    return q, c

# Compute lexical_context separately for every supervised causal prefix.
def score(h, q, c, candidate_ids):
    collaborative = dot(h, item_emb(candidate_ids))
    alpha = 2.0 * saved_A * sigmoid(amplitude_parameter)
    return collaborative + alpha * c * sparse_cosine(q, tfidf[candidate_ids])

# Host integration: preserve baseline loading, routing, checkpoints, and predictor API.
for condition in ['objective_only', 'starting_lexical', 'anchored_lexical']:
    for category in FOUR_BASELINE_CATEGORIES:
        reset_training_seed(42)
        initialize_same_sasrec_backbone()
        for batch in unchanged_category_loader(category):
            h = causal_sasrec_features(batch.sequence)
            q, c = causal_contexts(batch.sequence, anchored=(condition == 'anchored_lexical'))
            if condition == 'objective_only':
                c = zeros_like(c)
            candidates, mask = positive_plus_unique_uniform_negatives(
                count=32, exclude='padding,target,observed_prefix_only')
            logits = score(h, q, c, candidates)
            loss = masked_cross_entropy_over_eligible_positions(logits, mask, positive_index=0)
            optimize(loss)
            honor_baseline_checkpoints_and_remaining_budget()
        save_trial_local_artifacts_and_emit_matching_predictor()
        verify_predictor_parity_and_run_adapted_diagnostics()
# Host evaluates complete four-category conditions with unchanged pinned validation.
# Select highest macro HR@10; retain incumbent on ties. Never access hidden test labels.

originality.positive: Recent-anchor agreement supplies a small, explicit extension to repeated-support lexical fusion with a directly isolatable ablation.
originality.negative: Recency selection, historical-interest matching, lexical pooling, and gated additive scoring are established ideas; this is an incremental combination.

future_potential.positive: Separates repeated evidence from recent relevance and creates a simple baseline for later learned temporal routing.
future_potential.negative: Lexical agreement misses paraphrases and complements, repeated boilerplate can activate support, and abrupt recent purchases can suppress valid persistent interests.

code_difficulty.positive: Adds a fixed anchor-weight calculation to the starting scorer while retaining SASRec and its training pipeline.
code_difficulty.negative: Efficient sparse causal scoring, exact compatibility features, shared calibration, and generated-predictor parity still require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal self-attention recommendation backbone retained in this proposal.
limitations: Does not establish specific current usefulness, compatibility, or unmet needs from purchase histories.

related_work.title: ICSRec
contributions: The supplied search summary describes contrastive learning of latent intentions from sliding subsequences.
limitations: Same-target alignment is an assumption about shared intention; results do not establish gains under this pinned protocol.

related_work.title: Hierarchical long/short-term modeling
contributions: The supplied summary describes multiple historical preference vectors matched to recent interests with temporal information.
limitations: Learned routing adds complexity; the summary does not demonstrate that fixed recent lexical anchoring will improve this benchmark.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Motivates generalized BCE as a control for overconfidence associated with negative sampling.
limitations: An objective change alone does not explicitly address the diagnosed broad-association and stale-interest failures.

related_work.title: Sampled-softmax analysis
contributions: Connects sampled-softmax optimization to negative weighting and ranking behavior.
limitations: Does not establish improved macro HR@10 here or eliminate false negatives from implicit interaction data.
